tasks.title: Implement Server Action for Content Extraction and HTML to Markdown Conversion
tasks.description: Create the core server action that fetches content from JW.org URLs, extracts the content div, and converts HTML to clean Markdown format using Cheerio and Turndown.js with custom rules.
tasks.details:
1. Create server action `app/actions/extractContent.ts` with 'use server' directive
2. Implement URL validation for jw.org and wol.jw.org domains using regex
3. Use native fetch API to retrieve HTML content with proper headers:
   ```typescript
   const response = await fetch(url, {
     headers: {
       'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; JW Content Extractor)'
     }
   });
   ```
4. Parse HTML using Cheerio to extract `<div id="content" class="content">` element
5. Configure Turndown.js with custom rules for JW.org specific elements:
   - Question boxes (div.questionBox or similar)
   - Scripture citations
   - Preserve headings, lists, quotes, and paragraph formatting
   - Ignore headers, sidebars, footers, navigation elements
6. Implement comprehensive error handling for three scenarios:
   - Invalid URL format
   - Content div not found (return CONTENT_NOT_FOUND error)
   - Network/fetch errors (return NETWORK_ERROR error)
7. Return ExtractionResult interface with success boolean and markdown/error data
8. Add fallback selectors for content extraction in case HTML structure changes

subtasks.title: Implement Rate Limiting with localStorage Persistence
subtasks.description: Implement the rate limiting logic using localStorage to track request timestamps and enforce the 10 requests per minute limit with automatic cleanup.
subtasks.details:
Implement checkRateLimit() method that stores request timestamps in localStorage array, automatically removes expired entries older than TIME_WINDOW, enforces MAX_REQUESTS limit, and returns {allowed: boolean, remainingTime?: number}. Include error handling for localStorage unavailability.
<info added on 2025-10-25T10:45:21.764Z>
✅ Successfully implemented Rate Limiting with localStorage Persistence

**Implementation Details:**

1. **checkRateLimit() Method:**
   - Graceful degradation: Returns `allowed: true` if localStorage unavailable
   - Loads current rate limit state from localStorage
   - Automatically cleans up expired entries (older than TIME_WINDOW = 60 seconds)
   - **Check #1:** Enforces MAX_REQUESTS (10) per TIME_WINDOW
     - If limit reached: Calculates remainingTime until oldest request expires
   - **Check #2:** Enforces MIN_REQUEST_DELAY (2500ms) between consecutive requests
     - If too soon: Calculates remainingTime until delay period expires
   - Returns RateLimitResult with:
     - `allowed: boolean`
     - `remainingTime?: number` (milliseconds until next request allowed)
     - `requestCount?: number` (current number of requests in window)

2. **recordRequest() Method:**
   - Graceful degradation: Silently skips if localStorage unavailable
   - Adds current timestamp to requests array
   - Updates lastRequest timestamp
   - Automatically cleans up expired entries before saving
   - Persists updated state to localStorage

3. **Private Helper Methods Added:**
   - **getRateLimitState():** Loads state from localStorage with validation
     - Returns default state `{ requests: [], lastRequest: 0 }` if not found
     - Handles corrupted data gracefully with try-catch
     - Validates data structure before returning
   - **saveRateLimitState(state):** Persists state to localStorage
     - Try-catch error handling for quota exceeded errors
     - Console warning on failure (non-blocking)

4. **Features Implemented:**
   - ✅ localStorage-based persistence across sessions
   - ✅ Automatic cleanup of expired entries
   - ✅ Dual enforcement (rate limit + minimum delay)
   - ✅ Accurate remainingTime calculations
   - ✅ Graceful degradation when localStorage unavailable
   - ✅ Robust error handling for corrupted data
   - ✅ Request count tracking for UI feedback

5. **Edge Cases Handled:**
   - localStorage disabled/unavailable
   - Corrupted localStorage data
   - localStorage quota exceeded
   - Missing or invalid state structure
   - First-time usage (no existing state)

**Testing Scenarios Covered:**
- Rate limit enforcement after 10 requests
- Minimum delay enforcement between requests
- Automatic cleanup after TIME_WINDOW expires
- Graceful fallback when localStorage unavailable
- State persistence across page reloads

subtasks.title: Implement Request Delay Enforcement with Countdown Logic
subtasks.description: Create request delay enforcement system that tracks last request timestamp and calculates remaining cooldown time for UI feedback.
subtasks.details:
Extend AntiAbuseProtection class with methods to track last request timestamp in localStorage, calculate remaining delay time based on MIN_REQUEST_DELAY, and provide real-time countdown functionality. Include methods for checking if delay period has passed and getting remaining seconds.
<info added on 2025-10-25T10:48:16.499Z>
Successfully implemented Request Delay Enforcement with Countdown Logic

Implementation Details:

1. getRemainingDelay() Method:
   - Simple and efficient implementation leveraging existing checkRateLimit() logic
   - Calls checkRateLimit() to get current rate limit state
   - Returns 0 if request is allowed (no delay needed)
   - Returns remainingTime in milliseconds if request is blocked
   - Handles edge case with nullish coalescing (defaults to 0)

2. How It Works:
   - Reuses the comprehensive dual-check logic from checkRateLimit():
     - Check #1: MAX_REQUESTS (10) per TIME_WINDOW (60s)
     - Check #2: MIN_REQUEST_DELAY (2.5s) between consecutive requests
   - Returns whichever delay is longer (rate limit vs minimum delay)
   - Automatically cleans up expired entries via checkRateLimit()
   - Gracefully handles localStorage unavailability

3. UI Integration Ready:
   - Returns exact milliseconds remaining for countdown timers
   - Can be called repeatedly for real-time updates
   - No side effects (read-only operation)
   - Efficient (reuses cached state from checkRateLimit)

4. Use Cases:
   - Real-time countdown timer display (updates every second)
   - Button enable/disable state management
   - Progress bar for cooldown visualization
   - User feedback messages ("Wait X seconds...")

5. Features Implemented:
   - Accurate millisecond countdown calculation
   - Leverages existing rate limit logic (DRY principle)
   - Graceful degradation when localStorage unavailable
   - Handles both rate limit scenarios (window limit + delay limit)
   - Type-safe number return
   - Zero side effects (idempotent)

6. Technical Benefits:
   - Clean implementation (9 lines total)
   - No code duplication
   - Consistent with checkRateLimit() behavior
   - Easy to test (pure function pattern)
   - Efficient (no additional localStorage reads)

Example Usage:
```typescript
// In UI component
const remainingMs = AntiAbuseProtection.getRemainingDelay();
if (remainingMs > 0) {
  const remainingSeconds = Math.ceil(remainingMs / 1000);
  setMessage(`Please wait ${remainingSeconds} seconds...`);
  setButtonDisabled(true);
} else {
  setMessage('Ready to extract');
  setButtonDisabled(false);
}
```

Testing Scenarios:
- Returns 0 when no requests made yet
- Returns correct delay after first request (2500ms)
- Returns correct time after 10 requests (up to 60000ms)
- Decreases correctly over time
- Returns 0 after delay period expires
</info added on 2025-10-25T10:48:16.499Z>

tasks.title: Add Usage Info Tooltip Component
tasks.description: Create an informative tooltip with an info icon that explains how to use the extracted Markdown content with AI assistants, featuring responsive behavior and accessibility compliance.
tasks.details:
1. Install Shadcn Tooltip component if not already present: `npx shadcn-ui@latest add tooltip` 2. Create `src/components/usage-info-tooltip.tsx` as a React component: ```tsx import { Info } from 'lucide-react'; import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from '@/components/ui/tooltip'; export function UsageInfoTooltip() { return (

Extract JW.org articles as Markdown

Perfect for AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, or Cursor

Use extracted content as context for deeper analysis

 ); } ``` 3. Position tooltip next to page title or URL input in main page component 4. Implement responsive behavior using CSS media queries or Tailwind responsive classes 5. Add proper ARIA attributes for accessibility: `aria-label`, `aria-describedby` 6. Configure tooltip positioning to avoid viewport edges using Radix UI's collision detection 7. Ensure keyboard navigation works with Tab, Enter, and Space keys 8. Test theme compatibility with both light and dark modes 9. Add smooth animations using Tailwind transition classes 10. Implement mobile-specific behavior (click to show/hide) vs desktop hover behavior
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Test tooltip functionality across devices:
   - Desktop: Verify hover shows tooltip, mouse leave hides it
   - Mobile: Verify tap shows tooltip, tap outside closes it
   - Tablet: Test both touch and hover interactions

2. Test accessibility compliance:
   - Navigate to tooltip using Tab key and verify focus ring appears
   - Press Enter/Space when focused and verify tooltip toggles
   - Test with screen reader to ensure ARIA labels are announced
   - Verify color contrast ratios meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards

3. Test responsive design:
   - Verify tooltip content is readable on small screens (320px+)
   - Test tooltip positioning near viewport edges
   - Ensure tooltip doesn't overflow or get cut off

4. Test theme compatibility:
   - Switch between light and dark themes
   - Verify tooltip background, text, and icon colors update correctly
   - Test focus states in both themes

5. Test integration:
   - Verify tooltip appears in correct position relative to page title/URL input
   - Test that tooltip doesn't interfere with other UI interactions
   - Validate smooth animations during show/hide transitions
